title: De Proprietatibus Rerum - Medieval Manuscript
shelf_note: A 13th/14th-century two-column Latin textualis manuscript of Bartholomaeus Anglicus, book XIX (running head 'XIX'), on odour and stench. Its Smithsonian collection tag and the 1275 date are plausible.
structure_note: The structure counts give pages_translated 0, but the book field says 511 translated: the counts disagree. printed_backsteps 130 and printed_repeats 177 look like misreads, not a broken sequence. A manuscript foliated on rectos only will repeat or skip numbers. Marginal chapter numerals like '80' and '81' on this leaf could also be taken as page numbers. The OCR's <page-num>208 sits against a corner numeral I read as '209' (low confidence), which would make a misread numeral the source of some of these breaks.

pages.printed_marker: 209 (later-hand folio, top right; final digit uncertain); running head "XIX"; marginal chapter numbers "80" and "81"
pages.layout: two columns of textualis; red and blue initials and paragraph marks; rubricated running head; chapter numbers and one later-hand note in the margins

A raw '<column-break/>' sits in the middle of a sentence in the English ('brought to the organ <column-break/> and applied to it in taste')

items.quote: a garbled authority's name, possibly Isaac, who is cited on t

missing.english: It is a kind of altering species.
missing.why: 'species' here is the scholastic technical term (a sensible form passed to the sense organ), not a biological kind

missing.english: so a foul odor infects the spirit of smell and <unclear>troubles it</unclear>, as Ylaoch says
missing.why: The second 'Ylaoch' has no note; the reader is not told this is Isaac Israeli
'animal spirit' (spiritus animalis) is a term of Galenic physiology that a general reader will not know

missing.english: Inside the body, foul odor often arises from corrupted humor
missing.why: Humoral theory is assumed and never glossed

book_verdict: This is the right leaf of a real Bartholomaeus manuscript, and the translation is careful to mark its uncertain passages. But the OCR is badly garbled in places: 'Isaac' is read as 'Ylaoch', and the stench definition becomes a heading. The English also shows raw '->¶…<-' and '<column-break/>' markup to the reader.
